doc: I81 prereg instrument (BUILD_PLAN row I81 = I44a; whitepaper Def 6.13, Thm 6.8, Thm 6.9, Def 6.20, §10.10, §11.3 Impact column; the contract is the docstring of tests_m3/test_ranking.py). Frozen at the I81 prereg; the build reads it and never edits it. It fixes the policy the ranking applies, never a value: which measure each rule has (Def 6.13), the key a measure waits on when its rule or input does not exist yet, the sink class of each divergence channel, and the order of each ranking dimension (most severe first; the names inside one inner list share a rank). How a channel, a persistence class, a reach kind and a cost are computed from the records, witnesses, replay reports and model documents is the contract's rules K1-K8, PE1-PE3, RE1-RE3 and CO1; nothing here names a law, an action or a target. Amended at the I44 prereg (I44 = I44b, spec/M3/predictions/I44.json; the contract of the amendment is the docstring of tests_m3/test_measures_i44.py): NAT's measure is computed (its entry names a unit, the replay sub-directory whose runs hold the model's observations, and the observation, and no pending key), and the NAT entry of pending_measures is removed, since I29 (918b9a4e) brought rule NAT. Every other field is I81's, unchanged. Amended again at I44's stage 2, after I84 and I89 landed, as the contract's stage-2 clauses say: FACT's public_input sub-form is measured from its records (recorded), F(PI, parent lbn) leaves pending_measures; F(Z, derivation) leaves pending_measures for `pairs` (the product's FACT laws); DISCH stays pending, its why updated.

NAT.name: naturality_defect_mass
NAT.observation: the square's observation (I29's claim): the end version, the success of each step the two sides share (the migration and the op), and each storage word either end state holds, an absent word being the zero word

FACT.name: adversarial_freedom
FACT.recorded_scope: the decider's own measure of the field the public input leaves free, recorded with its kernel-checked witness (I84's rules)
FACT.why_not: an attribution law relates the principal whose bond a call puts at risk to the chooser of the content; it states no kernel pair (m, c), so Thm 6.8's F(m, c) has no instance

DISCH.name: discharge_profile
DISCH.why: a profile is a Pareto set over (cost, delay) of the strategies that discharge a guard (Def 6.20). I37's calibrated cost landed with I84 (= I37b): App. D's c0 + c1 * k gas for one action's backlog loop; it prices no discharging strategy of any other guard, and I84's self_controlled law is UNKNOWN (its k* lies beyond the kernel budget). No M3 law states a strategy's (cost, delay) point (I32's profile laws run on T32), so only I32's class exists. Which key brings M3 profiles is open (BUILD_PLAN I32 as built: the delay guard's M3 profile follows I36)

pairs.why: the plan-stated product laws over the Solidity commit and the Go derivation (I88, decided by I89); a FACT law there states the kernel pair (what the commitment binds, what the derivation derives). I26 took F(Z, derivation) as the maximum over its kernel laws, with the delivered blob list standing for the derivation; this is the maximum over the product's FACT laws, with the Go derivation itself

cost.counts: the state-changing calls of the witness schedule (calls of view or pure actions, and migrate steps, are not counted)

order_doc: Sink: the classes §11.3 names, by severity (funds and safety first, an off-chain view last); undecided last. Persistence (§10.10: discharge profiles feed it; a mixed profile ranks below a non-dischargeable one): a pure-function defect (code) and a non-dischargeable guard persist until the code changes; an undecided class ranks right below them, since it may be either; then the classes a principal can discharge, the self-dischargeable last. Reach: the obstruction reachable by anyone first; an undecided or pending reach right below it (it may be anyone's); then by the privilege the witness needs, the most privileged last. Cost: fewer calls first; an unknown cost last. Ties: the law id.
